Bitmine是美股那批“企业囤币”玩家里的ETH版，套路跟当年MicroStrategy囤BTC一模一样：发股融资，然后拿钱买币入账。根据CoinTelegraph报道，他们已经连续14个月按既定节奏买入ETH，目前正接近最初设定的囤币目标线。这次ETH放量突破$2,500，等于把这些企业财库的账面浮盈直接做实了一波，市场注意力重新回到“机构化囤ETH”这条叙事上。

对市场的影响
- 短期：ETH现价$2,508.26，24h涨2.57%，突破2.5K这个心理关口后，企业买盘成为持续性的需求方。跟散户追涨不同，Bitmine这类买家是纪律性买入，不管价格只按节奏囤，等于给市场提供了长期底仓吸筹。BTC在$79,629.67同步走强（+3.03%），整体风险偏好在回升。
- 中期：如果囤币目标达成后再加码，说明企业层面对ETH的配置逻辑从“试水”转向“战略持仓”，会带动更多上市公司复制这个模板。

一句话翻译：ETH这波不只是散户FOMO，背后有公司真金白银在持续接货。

我的判断
我看多，但不是无脑多。2.5K这个位置很关键——之前多次冲击未果，这次放量站稳，短期动能是实的。ETH若能守住$2,500上方，下一个阻力区间在$2,508.26-2,650一带；回踩不破2.45K则突破有效。风险点在于：如果Bitmine们达标后停止买入，这部分边际买盘消失，涨势的燃料会少一格。仓位重的注意波动，别把突破当单边保证。

I always thought it was the Zhuang [market maker] washing the order book. But actually, you should first think about which group you belong to.

When that long bullish candle pushed the price up, I was thinking about one question.

If I were the Zhuang, who would I sell this batch of coins to?

$BTC is now 79,378. It’s up 2.53% over the past 24 hours, with trading volume of 1.810 billion USDT.

A volume of 1.8 billion at this price level isn’t that big.

Dump it? Retail traders wouldn’t dare to buy it, and you won’t be able to sell at a good price.

Pump it? But then you’re afraid of feeding the short-term traders.

The best approach is to grind the price slowly—until you all feel it’s stable—then hand the goods over.

That’s what today’s BTC is like: grinding until people have no temper left.

If you look at the chart from the counterparty’s perspective, many moves suddenly make sense.

As for who’s counting their money, we’ll see after the close.

# I turned off my AI trading assistant for 7 days, and surprisingly I made 61% fewer trades—meaning I’m getting “cut” worse than I imagined

I turned off my AI trading assistant for 7 days, and my number of trades actually dropped by 61%.
What’s even more painful is that the account’s fluctuations became noticeably smaller too. The issue probably was never “I can’t analyze.”

Last month, I did a pretty crude real-world test: for two consecutive weeks, I recorded the time of each screen check—asking the AI, placing orders, and canceling them. In the first week, I used it normally: I sent the AI K-line screenshots and asked it to explain trends, support/resistance, and sentiment. In the second week, I completely shut off the assistant and kept only a handwritten checklist: why I’m looking, what conditions make me act, and what situations mean I immediately give up.

In week one, I checked the market 43 times and actually executed 18 trades. Of those 18 trades, 11 happened after the AI gave answers like “slightly bullish but needs confirmation” or “there’s an opportunity for a short-term move.” Looking back, those kinds of replies didn’t directly tell me to buy—but they gave me a dangerous psychological permission. If the model also sees an opportunity, then trying it seems reasonable. As a result, many of the trades weren’t wrong because my judgment was off—they failed because there were no clear invalidation conditions. The price would move, and the script would change instantly.

In week two, I checked the market 19 times and executed 7 trades. The most effective part wasn’t simply skipping a few charts—it was forcing myself to fill in three fields before taking action: the trigger condition, the maximum loss I can tolerate, and the falsification signal. For example, when observing $BTC , I stopped asking “should I buy right now?” Instead, I only let the AI refute my logic. When looking at $ETH , I also only asked it to list the data I ignored and the contrary scenarios. The AI went from being a judge to being a sparring partner. Hallucinations and ambiguity weren’t as easy to turn into actual positions.

This test confirmed one thing for me: AI is best at expanding information, not at helping you carry risk. It can list five possibilities in ten seconds, but it won’t pay for any of them. A truly useful way to use it is to have it find flaws, organize logs, and review repeated mistakes—not to generate a comforting directional judgment.

At this point, I even save every AI suggestion along with the subsequent price movement, and at the end of the month I’ll specifically统计 the hit rate of the answers that sounded the most confident. The sample size is still small, but there’s already a pattern: the more complete the wording, the less it necessarily means the evidence is stronger.

When you got cut the worst by AI trading advice—was it because the AI was wrong, or because you treated a vague answer as certainty?

# 我把 AI 交易助手关了 7 天，交易次数反而少了 61%，这意味着我被割得比想象中更惨

我把 AI 交易助手关了 7 天，交易次数反而少了 61%。
更扎心的是：账户波动也明显变小，问题可能从来不是“不会分析”。

上个月我做了一次很土的实测：连续两周记录每次打开行情、问 AI、下单和撤单的时间。第一周照常使用，把 K 线截图丢给 AI，让它解释趋势、支撑阻力和情绪；第二周彻底关掉助手，只保留一张纸质清单：为什么看、什么条件才行动、什么情况立即放弃。

第一周共看盘 43 次，实际操作 18 次，其中 11 次发生在 AI 给出“偏多但需确认”或“短线存在机会”之后。回头看，这类回答没有直接叫我买，却给了我一种危险的心理许可：既然模型也看到了机会，那试一点似乎很合理。结果不少操作不是判断错，而是根本没有明确的失效条件，价格一晃就改剧本。

第二周只看盘 19 次，操作 7 次。最有效的不是少看几张图，而是强迫自己在行动前写满三格：触发条件、最大可承受损失、证伪信号。比如观察 $BTC 时，我不再问“现在该不该买”，而是只让 AI 反驳我的逻辑；看 $ETH 时，也只让它列出我忽略的数据和相反情景。AI 从裁判变成陪练，幻觉和模棱两可就没那么容易变成仓位。

这次测试让我确认一件事：AI 最擅长扩展信息，不擅长替你承担风险。它能在十秒内列出五种可能，却不会为其中任何一种付钱。真正有用的用法，是让它挑漏洞、整理日志、复盘重复犯错，而不是生成一句让人心安的方向判断。

我现在甚至会保存每次 AI 建议和后续走势，月底专门统计“听起来最自信”的回答命中率。样本还不大，但已有一个规律：措辞越完整，不等于证据越充分。

你被 AI 交易建议割得最惨的一次，是它判断错了，还是你把模糊回答当成了确定性？

50% tariffs on Canadian goods, effective only in 2027—why are they shaking BTC right now?

💡 Bearish for BTC/ETH: escalating trade tensions directly hit risk appetite.

Trump announced 50% tariffs on Canadian cars and steel starting January 1, 2027. Supply-chain costs rise, which is bearish for crypto and other risk assets.

What’s going on
Trump plans to impose an additional 50% tariff on cars and steel imported from Canada starting January 1, 2027. Although that date is more than a year away, markets won’t wait until then to react. The U.S. and Canada are among each other’s biggest trade partners, and the auto and steel supply chains are deeply intertwined. A 50% tariff is basically equivalent to rerunning the bookkeeping of that entire supply chain. The outcome can only be two things: supply-chain disruption and higher prices for consumer goods. Once inflation expectations start rising, the room for the Federal Reserve to cut rates gets squeezed—an outcome that the most liquidity-sensitive crypto market definitely doesn’t want.

In one sentence: the tariffs themselves won’t take effect until 2027, but inflation expectations start getting priced in today.

Market impact
- Short term: Trade-tension sentiment directly suppresses risk appetite. BTC rose only 1.40% around $78,542, indicating capital is hesitant. ETH at $2,493 and XRP both fell 2.04%—altcoins are already signaling. Safe-haven capital is more inclined to wait and see rather than chase higher prices.
- Medium term: If inflation picks up due to tariffs and the pace of rate cuts slows, the macro tailwind for crypto turns into a headwind. Since it’s effective in 2027, this is a prolonged battle, not a one-time shock.

My take
Slightly bearish in the short term. This bounce in BTC to $78,542 couldn’t hold a breakout. The tariff news gives the bulls a reason to take profits. Support to watch is around $76,000; if that breaks, it could pull back to $73,000. ETH is weaker relative to BTC, with only a 1.41% rebound. If BTC slips, ETH’s losses will very likely be amplified. Before the tariffs take effect, every escalation in trade tensions acts as a stress test. Key risk: if negotiations later ease, sentiment could flip quickly.

🎯 Impact forecast
- Coins: BTC / ETH
- Direction: Bearish 📉 forecast a drop
- Duration: BTC 12 hours / ETH 24 hours

title: Ethereum $2,500 Battle: Can ETH Turn Resistance Into the Next Major Rally?
subTitle:
Ethereum is back in the spotlight as ETH continues to trade around the psychologically important $2,500 level. After a powerful recovery, the market is now asking one major question: Can Ethereum turn $2,500 from resistance into support and continue higher?
Ethereum previously crossed $2,500 on August 21, with Binance reporting ETH trading around $2,503.93 after a strong 24-hour move. � Since then, ETH has pulled back toward the $2,400–$2,500 area, making this level an important battleground for bulls and bears.
Binance
🚀 ETH's Recovery Has Changed the Market Mood
The recent Ethereum recovery has been one of the most noticeable moves in the crypto market. ETH has climbed sharply from its August lows, attracting renewed attention from traders and investors.
Current market data shows ETH trading close to the $2,500 region, while recent price action has repeatedly tested the area around this psychological resistance. �
MetaMask +1
The significance of $2,500 goes beyond a simple round number. It represents an area where sellers have previously appeared, meaning a clean breakout and successful retest could give buyers additional confidence.
If ETH can establish several candles above this level rather than simply making a temporary spike, the market could begin treating $2,500 as a new support zone.
That would potentially open the door for the next major move.
🐂 Bulls Have Several Reasons to Stay Optimistic
One of the strongest arguments for Ethereum bulls is the improvement in institutional demand.
Recent data showed that U.S. spot Ethereum ETFs attracted approximately $697.2 million during the five trading sessions through August 21, while Bitcoin ETFs brought in approximately $1.918 billion. Together, the two markets recorded their strongest weekly inflows of 2026. �
CryptoSlate
ETF flows matter because they provide a channel through which traditional investors can gain exposure to crypto without directly holding the underlying asset.
If strong inflows continue, they could provide an important source of demand for ETH.
Another bullish development is continued accumulation by large corporate holders.
BitMine recently purchased approximately 32,447 ETH worth around $81.2 million, its largest single-week addition since early July, according to reporting cited by CoinDesk. �
CoinDesk +1
Large purchases do not guarantee that ETH will rise, but they can strengthen the broader narrative that major investors remain interested in Ethereum at current levels.
⚠️ The $2,500 Level Is Still a Major Test
Despite the bullish momentum, traders should not assume that breaking $2,500 automatically means ETH will immediately enter a new parabolic rally.
The market has already shown that $2,500 can attract selling pressure.
Recent technical analysis places the area around $2,500–$2,600 as an important resistance region. �
CryptoRank
This means ETH may need to consolidate around $2,400–$2,500 before attempting another breakout.
A strong move above $2,500 followed by a successful retest would be considerably more convincing than a quick wick above the level followed by a sharp rejection.
For bulls, the ideal scenario would look something like this:
Break $2,500 → Hold $2,500 → Retest $2,500 → Continue higher.
That type of structure could attract momentum traders and potentially accelerate the next leg upward.
🎯 What Could Be the Next ETH Targets?
If Ethereum successfully breaks and holds above $2,500, traders will likely begin watching the next resistance zones.
The first major area could be around $2,600. A sustained move above $2,600 would strengthen the breakout and could shift attention toward the $2,700 area.
Some current market analysis has identified approximately $2,700 as a potential upside target if ETH can maintain support around the low-$2,400s. �
TMGM
A stronger continuation could eventually bring the $2,800–$3,000 zone into focus.
However, these are potential technical levels—not guaranteed targets.
Crypto markets can move extremely quickly, especially after large rallies. Traders should therefore avoid treating price targets as promises.
🛡️ What If Ethereum Gets Rejected?
The bearish scenario is equally important.
If ETH repeatedly fails to break $2,500 and starts losing momentum, sellers could push the price back toward the lower support zones.
One important area to watch is around $2,350–$2,400. Recent analysis has identified approximately $2,356 as an important support level beneath the current market area. �
CoinDCX
A drop below that zone would weaken the immediate bullish structure and could indicate that the $2,500 breakout attempt was unsuccessful.
The key distinction is between a normal pullback and a trend reversal.
A controlled pullback that holds above major support could simply give buyers another opportunity to enter.
But if ETH begins making lower highs and lower lows while losing important support levels, traders may need to reconsider the bullish setup.
📊 ETH vs. Bitcoin: Why Ethereum Is Getting Attention
Bitcoin remains the dominant cryptocurrency, but Ethereum has recently shown impressive momentum.
The broader crypto market has benefited from renewed ETF demand, improving liquidity expectations and a weaker-dollar narrative. Bitcoin and Ethereum both experienced strong moves as investors returned to risk assets. �
CoinDesk
For Ethereum, however, the $2,500 breakout gives the market a clear technical story.
Traders now have an obvious level to watch.
Above $2,500: bullish confirmation.
Below $2,500: resistance remains active.
That simplicity can itself generate additional trading interest because both bulls and bears have a clearly defined battlefield.
🔥 The Biggest Question for ETH Traders
The biggest question is no longer whether Ethereum can reach $2,500.
It already did.
The question now is whether Ethereum can stay above $2,500 and turn the level into support.
That distinction is extremely important.
A temporary breakout can be caused by short-term momentum, leveraged positions or sudden buying pressure. A sustainable breakout usually requires follow-through.
If ETH can hold above $2,500 while trading volume remains strong and ETF demand continues, the probability of another upside attempt could increase.
On the other hand, if buyers repeatedly fail to defend the level, the market could enter another consolidation phase.
🚨 Final Takeaway
Ethereum has entered an important phase.
The recent rally, renewed ETF inflows and large ETH purchases have improved the bullish narrative. ETF data showed nearly $700 million of weekly inflows into Ethereum funds, while BitMine's latest purchase demonstrates continued interest from large holders. �
CryptoSlate +1
But the market still needs confirmation.
$2,500 is the key level.
A clean breakout and successful retest could put $2,600, $2,700 and potentially $2,800+ on the radar.
A rejection, however, could send ETH back toward the $2,350–$2,400 support area.
For traders, the smartest approach may be to watch the reaction around $2,500 rather than chase a sudden green candle.
Ethereum is not simply testing a price—it is testing market confidence.
If bulls win this battle and turn $2,500 into support, ETH could be setting up for another major move.
If bears defend the level, the market may need more time to build momentum.
The next few sessions could determine whether $2,500 becomes Ethereum's launchpad—or its ceiling.

title: 📊 ÚLTIMA SEMANA DE AGOSTO: REGULAÇÃO, JACKSON HOLE E A OFERTA DE TOKENS QUE VEM PELA FRENTE
subTitle:
📊 ÚLTIMA SEMANA DE AGOSTO: REGULAÇÃO, JACKSON HOLE E A OFERTA DE TOKENS QUE VEM PELA FRENTE
Fechamos agosto com o mercado cripto navegando entre dois sinais: o regulatório, lento mas em movimento real, e o de curto prazo, com eventos macro e desbloqueios de token concentrados nesta última semana do mês.

🏛️ O RCA: A SEC propõe um caminho mais claro
A SEC apresentou o Regulation Crypto Assets (RCA), pacote que cria vias específicas de oferta para tokens, em vez de depender só de formulários tradicionais ou de ações de execução caso a caso. Na prática: isenção para startups captarem até US$ 5 milhões em quatro anos, com divulgações no próprio site, além de faixas escalonadas de até US$ 20 milhões (Tier 1) e US$ 75 milhões (Tier 2) por ano, com exigências crescentes de reporte.
O detalhe mais relevante é o “porto seguro” condicional: quando o trabalho essencial de um projeto estiver concluído e a rede for suficientemente descentralizada, a venda contínua do token pode deixar de ser tratada como valor mobiliário. Isso tende a beneficiar ecossistemas com grande volume de lançamentos, como Ethereum e Solana, dando critério mais objetivo sobre quando um token “se descola” do status de security.
Mas atenção: o RCA ainda não é lei. Falta consulta pública de cerca de 60 dias e redação final da SEC. Em paralelo, o Congresso avalia o Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, mais amplo, que definiria a divisão de competências entre SEC e CFTC — com votação de cloture no Senado no radar.

📅 O que movimenta esta semana
Jackson Hole (27-29/ago): principal evento do Fed no ano, com poder real de mexer expectativa de juros e apetite por risco global.
PIB e PCE dos EUA: inflação e atividade econômica seguem como termômetro para leitura de política monetária — e, por tabela, para BTC e altcoins.
Resultado da Nvidia: mesmo sendo ação, costuma contaminar o humor de todo o setor de tecnologia e risco, cripto incluso.

⚠️ Desbloqueios de token — a semana mais pesada de agosto
Entre 24 e 30/08, estima-se cerca de US$ 706 milhões em emissões na semana. Cliff unlocks mais concentrados: Humanity (H) com ~US$ 18,53 mi (13,4% do supply liberado), Huma Finance (HUMA) com ~US$ 9,89 mi (26,5% de impacto — o mais sensível da lista), Plasma (XPL) com ~US$ 8,85 mi (3,3%) e SosoValue (SOSO) com ~US$ 7,32 mi (6,9%).
Nas emissões lineares diárias, destaque para BTC (~US$ 33,75 mi/dia), RAIN (~US$ 18,40 mi/dia), ETH (~US$ 6,38 mi/dia) e SOL (~US$ 6,02 mi/dia) — efeito mais diluído, mas relevante em momentos de sensibilidade de mercado. Vale o alerta técnico: unlock grande não é sinônimo automático de queda. O que importa é quem recebe (time, investidores, comunidade), qual fatia representa da oferta circulante, e a liquidez do ativo. Por isso HUMA, com 26,5% de impacto relativo, tende a pesar mais que XPL, mesmo com valor absoluto menor.

🔍 No radar cripto
Força recente do ETH segue sustentando o sentimento do mercado; o ataque à ponte Allbridge reacendeu discussão sobre risco em soluções cross-chain, tema sensível sempre que envolve movimentação de valor entre redes diferentes

🔮 O que esperar para setembro
Setembro chega como mês de definição em três frentes: o tom de Jackson Hole vai calibrar a expectativa de juros pro resto do ano; a consulta pública do RCA deve avançar, testando se a proposta sai como está ou sofre revisão; e o Senado pode finalmente votar o CLARITY Act, resolvendo (ou não) parte da incerteza sobre quem regula o quê no setor.

BTC breaks through $79,000, but the whale Machi fully closes long positions: take profit of $333,000 or run early?
After BTC broke through $79,000, the well-known whale Machi cleared all his BTC long positions and exited with profits. His remaining positions are still heavily weighted toward ETH-based altcoins.

On-chain analyst Ai Yi reported that after BTC broke through $79,000, the famous whale Machi (Big Brother) closed all his Bitcoin long positions, realizing a $333,000 profit, and also reduced a portion of the longs in three other tokens. But he wasn’t fully out of the market—he still holds three positions: ETH, HYPE, and PUMP, with a total value of $94.92 million and an unrealized profit of more than $2.88 million. In plain terms: partial profit-taking on BTC, while the altcoin positions continue to be held.

Impact on the market
- Short term: The amount involved in this BTC fully-closing move is not large by Machi’s scale (a $333,000 profit is just a rounding error for a whale of this size). The signaling matters more than the actual sell pressure. At present BTC is around $78,256; after breaking $79,000, a small pullback is normal digestion. The remaining $94.92M is concentrated in ETH/HYPE/PUMP, suggesting that the “smart money” has shifted its focus from BTC to altcoins to catch up on gains.
- Medium term: After breaking a key level, the whale doesn’t chase price higher—but also doesn’t withdraw the altcoin positions. This structure is relatively friendly for the outlook. If they were truly bearish, they wouldn’t keep nearly a billion dollars’ worth of unrealized profit to ride out volatility.

My view
I’m leaning bullish. The logic is simple: Machi closing his BTC longs looks more like position rebalancing than a directional reversal—the remaining $94.92M in altcoins is the real stance. Once BTC stands above $79,000 and holds the pullback to $78,256, the short-term structure is still likely dominated by bulls. The area above $79,000 turns into resistance; if price then holds above it on strong volume, it opens up new upside space.

The risk is this: if the remaining positions—like ETH and HYPE—start being reduced quickly, then it means the whale may have truly exited, and the assessment would need to be redone. Current data does not support that scenario.

⚠️ The most important skill in trading contracts isn’t prediction—it’s admitting when you’re wrong.
Many people’s biggest problem in contracts is this:
After going long and it drops—
“Wait a bit, it’ll bounce back soon.”
After going short and it rises—
“It’s already gone up so much; it can’t keep going up.”
After the stop-loss is hit—
“Let it loosen a bit more; wait for it to come back.”
In the end, a small loss that could have been acceptable gets dragged into a heavy-position loss, even to the point of liquidation.
Wrong is wrong.
Trading isn’t an exam—no one requires you to be correct on every trade.
Truly mature traders allow themselves to make mistakes, but never allow one mistake to expand without limit.
If your logic for opening the position fails, you should exit.
What if the market moves back after the stop-loss?
No problem.
If you stop out and it was a wrong stop, you just lose a small amount;
if you “hold the position” when you’re wrong, you might lose your next chance to trade.
Don’t try to prove “I’m right” by fighting the market.
The market won’t care about your entry price.
And it won’t reverse just because you’re down and how much you’ve lost.
The mindset that contract trading truly requires is:
Before opening a position, figure out exactly where you’re wrong.
At that level, execute the stop-loss.
After the stop-loss, re-analyze.
When a new opportunity appears, re-enter.
One trade wrong isn’t scary.
What’s truly terrifying is—
Knowing you’re wrong, yet still turning the trade into gambling because you can’t accept it.
Remember:
Timely stop-loss isn’t failure—it’s preserving your capital for the next opportunity.
Stay alive first, then talk about profit.

很多人做合约最大的毛病就是：
开多之后跌了——
“再等等，马上反弹。”
开空之后涨了——
“已经涨这么多了，不可能继续涨。”
止损到了——
“再放宽一点，等它回来。”
最后，一笔原本可以接受的小亏损，硬生生拖成重仓亏损，甚至爆仓。
错了就是错了。
交易不是考试，没有人要求你每一单都判断正确。
真正成熟的交易者允许自己犯错，但绝不允许一个错误无限扩大。
你开仓的逻辑失效了，就应该离场。
止损以后行情又走回来？
没关系。
止损错了，你只是亏一笔小钱；
扛单错了，你可能失去下一次交易的资格。
不要为了证明“我是对的”，去和市场较劲。
市场不会在乎你的开仓价，更不会因为你亏了多少就一定反转。
合约交易真正需要建立的思维是：
开仓之前想清楚哪里错。
到了那个位置，执行止损。
止损之后，重新分析。
出现新的机会，再重新进场。
一单错了不可怕。
真正可怕的是——
明明知道错了，却因为不甘心，把交易做成了赌博。
记住：
及时止损不是失败，而是在为下一次机会保留本金。
先活下来，再谈利润。

title: Ethereum's Explosive Short Squeeze: What's Behind ETH's Surge Toward $2,500
subTitle:
Ethereum just delivered one of its most dramatic moves of the year, surging roughly 31% in a single week and reclaiming levels not seen since before the summer selloff. For traders, this squeeze-driven rally is packed with signals worth unpacking.
The Numbers Right Now
ETH has climbed from under $1,900 to a recent intraday peak near $2,500, with price now consolidating in that zone. The move has cleared every major moving average on the daily chart, and the 50-day EMA has crossed above the 100-day EMA — a structural signal that often points to further upside if it holds.
What's Fueling the Move
1. A historic short squeeze — Weekly short liquidations have averaged over $130 million, forcing leveraged bears to cover and adding fuel to the rally. However, spot demand has remained somewhat tentative, meaning much of this move is derivatives-driven rather than pure organic buying.
2. ETF inflows returning — After outflows earlier in the summer, Ethereum ETFs pulled in roughly $700 million in a single week, reversing a multi-hundred-million-dollar outflow from the prior week.
3. Recovery from a rough patch — ETH endured a steep June crash tied to Ethereum Foundation restructuring news and ETF outflows, followed by a steady summer recovery as institutional money slowly returned.
4. Whale accumulation — Large holders have reportedly been withdrawing ETH from exchanges, reducing available sell-side supply and reinforcing a bullish structural case.
What Traders Should Watch
Key resistance: The $2,500 level has already rejected price once this session. A monthly close above it would help confirm the breakout is being absorbed rather than sold into.
Support to watch: Losing $2,356 opens a retest of the 20-day EMA near $2,090; a break below the 200-day EMA at roughly $2,136 would call the entire breakout into question.
Overbought signals: RSI has been sitting near 78, suggesting a near-term pullback or consolidation is likely even within an intact uptrend.
Mixed positioning: While some large market makers have been increasing short bets, others point to bullish accumulation — a reminder that conviction is split even among sophisticated players.
Security headlines: A recently disclosed wallet app bug is a reminder to stay alert to security news, which can shift sentiment quickly regardless of price action.
The Bigger Picture
Ethereum remains the second-largest cryptocurrency by market cap, and its role as a decentralized computing platform — not just a currency — continues to differentiate it from Bitcoin. ETH is still trading well below its all-time high from 2025, so this rally, however sharp, is best read as one chapter in a longer, more volatile story. Whether the squeeze extends into a sustained trend or fades into consolidation, risk management stays essential in a market capable of moving 20%+ in a matter of days.

We guided two more tubes; they were very thin, like the rice porridge from a cup that cost five mao at the school gate twelve years ago.
After we finished our morning exercises, we passed by the shopfront and talked about what we would use our ideals to do in the future.
The dust and mist hadn’t cleared yet.
In the plastic tubes, what lay there looked like a thread of dawn light, diluted by water.
The aunt who sold porridge always smiled, adding a little more sugar into each cup.
Back then, we thought life would always be this sweet.
On some morning many years later,
I stood in front of the bathroom mirror and squeezed toothpaste.
Suddenly I saw those white paste-like blobs—so much like the congealed rice slurry back then.
Amid the buzzing hum of the electric toothbrush,
I could clearly hear someone on the other side of the mist ask: “Where did you plant your ideals afterward?”
And the answer was already flowing away in silence along the drain.

BTC hits $79,989—options traders go wild, betting $100,000: Is this a leveraged bull run accelerating, or a top signal?

During the day, BTC briefly touched $79,989. Call options and futures open interest both surged, and the derivatives market is starting to price in the $100,000 mark.

Everyone on the street is clear about this: BTC spot once reached $79,989, with the current price at $79,078.01 and up 2.28% over the past 24 hours. But what really matters isn’t spot—it’s derivatives. Traders have stacked billions of dollars in positions across futures and options, and they’re willing to pay increasingly expensive premiums to chase higher strike prices. That suggests the market isn’t just rising—it’s rising with leverage. Futures open interest (OI) accelerates upward along with the price action. The call option side is especially aggressive, with large bets already placed on strike prices at $100,000.

Impact on the market
- Short term: Higher premium spending for buying calls boosts implied volatility. Market makers hedging will keep buying spot, creating a positive feedback loop. Accelerating OI buildup means the trend has fuel—but it also means an imbalance between longs and shorts. If a pullback occurs, the liquidation cascade could be amplified by leverage.
- Mid term: The $100,000 level is shifting from a “forward-looking narrative” into a price consensus. Capital will continue moving from sidelines into trend-following positions. Derivatives overheating by itself isn’t necessarily a top—but historically, periods of accelerating leverage often correspond to the latter half of a move.

My take
Clearly bullish, but with caution. The trend is upward, and real-money option capital is on the line. There’s no sign yet that short-term momentum has fully exhausted. The intraday high of $79,989 is the nearest resistance level; once it holds, $100,000 is more of a psychological threshold. Downside support is in the area where OI is densely piled up. If the pullback doesn’t break that, the structure isn’t broken.

There’s only one key risk: the higher the leverage density, the deeper a flash crash. Awareness of position size matters more than direction.

As the U.S. moves to isolate Iran, why did BTC first rise 2%?

As the U.S. escalates pressure on Iran and geopolitical risk heats up, BTC strengthened at $78,981, with the “safe-haven” narrative returning.

The U.S. announced a new round of “isolation actions” against the Iranian regime, covering both diplomatic and economic fronts. In plain terms, it’s the coalition of allies pushing Iran further out of the international system. The update also makes one thing clear: this move could effectively shut the door on future diplomatic negotiations—there will be fewer paths to de-escalation, meaning geopolitical tension is likely to last longer rather than be digested quickly.

What’s interesting is the market reaction: BTC rose 2.03% in 24 hours to $78,981.99, ETH gained 1.26% to $2,480.14, while XRP fell 2.26%—clearly indicating funds are rotating toward larger coins.

Impact on the market
- Short term: Historically, escalating geopolitical conflict has been a double-edged sword for BTC. But this move shows capital is treating it as a “de-sovereignized” asset. Beyond traditional safe havens (gold, U.S. Treasuries), some hot money directly flowed into BTC. High-beta altcoins like XRP were bled off (-2.26%), which is typical “risk-on” rotation rather than broad-based gains.
- Medium term: If the isolation actions continue to escalate and diplomatic channels close, the market will likely reprice a “long-term uncertainty premium.” That would provide ongoing narrative support for BTC.

One-line translation: The messier the world gets, the more people realize they need an asset that doesn’t depend on any government.

My take
The direction is clear: bullish on BTC in the short term. The logic is simple—geopolitical tension + verified capital flows, and the price has already cast a vote with a 2% rise. Key support is around the $78,000 level; if it holds, there’s a chance to challenge the $80,000 psychological round number. ETH is also moving up, but with weaker elasticity than BTC. In this setup, don’t expect a broad altcoin rally—fund concentration will be higher. The key risk is: if the U.S. and Iran suddenly send signals of de-escalation, the safe-haven premium could be rapidly unwound, and the upside may narrow just as quickly.

When someone at the Speaker’s level talks publicly about a “new phase,” it’s basically laying the groundwork for a larger-scale military intervention. Ally involvement means the conflict is evolving from a Middle East localized incident into a geopolitical crisis involving multiple countries—something the market fears most: the spillover of uncertainty.

Impact on the market
- Short term: Escalating geopolitical tensions first hit risk appetite. BTC is now $77,218.13 and is down only 0.11% over 24h—looking stable, but this “calm before the storm” is the most dangerous. In plain terms, it’s tightening the door to the dollar system another notch: any entity deemed to have helped launder money for Iran will have SWIFT and dollar clearing cut off as well. The exact enforcement and coverage of these sanctions hasn’t been detailed yet, but the direction is already clear.

Circle’s share price jumped 30% in one day, as capital re-priced the stablecoin sector—an overall positive for the entire Crypto market.

The market re-ran the numbers and found that the valuation previously assigned to Circle was too low.

In one sentence: it’s not that Circle got stronger—Wall Street finally admits that stablecoins are a cash cow you can actually balance the books on.

Short term: direct positive on sentiment. The stablecoin narrative is a leading indicator for capital flowing back into Crypto. What are gas fees?

Every transaction or operation on Ethereum requires computational resources.

The fee paid for using those resources is called a gas fee, and it is paid in ETH.

For example, you might pay ETH to:

* Send tokens
* Interact with a DeFi application
* Buy an NFT
* Execute a smart contract

Gas fees can change depending on network demand.

4. DeFi — ETH is used throughout decentralized finance applications.

6. Smart contracts — ETH helps power transactions and applications using Ethereum smart contracts.

$ETH #ETH In a strong trend, pullbacks often reveal real underlying demand better than a sharp acceleration upward. The current 1-hour change is +0.51% and the 24-hour change is +2.28%, so we need to judge whether this is a normal cooldown or a weakening structure.

With the current 1-hour +0.51% and 24-hour +2.28%, the two timeframes have not yet formed a sufficiently clear same-direction confirmation. In a range-bound market, chasing strength and selling weakness has a low margin for error. It is better to use the upper boundary to confirm direction, the lower boundary to confirm support, and the midpoint only as a dividing line between strength and weakness.

Short-term control has not been clearly broken, and 2,478.84 is the primary standard for judging pullback quality. Holding above it and then retesting 2,532.95 would indicate a relatively strong consolidation; if price breaks below the midpoint and stays there, attention should shift down to 2,424.73.

There are three possible ways to handle the next path: if price breaks above and holds firmly above 2,532.95, wait for a pullback that does not break down before reassessing continuation; if it falls below 2,424.73, prioritize risk control and wait for new support; if it continues to oscillate around 2,478.84, treat it as range rotation and avoid repeatedly chasing direction in the middle.

Position management should distinguish between spot and contracts. Existing spot positions can be managed in stages around key levels, without frequently switching direction based on a single 1-hour candlestick; waiting for confirmation with no position is more flexible and measured. Contracts should place greater emphasis on entry level and invalidation conditions; when volatility expands, actively reduce size to avoid turning a short-term judgment into passive holding.

Risk control still comes before conclusions: act only when conditions are met, and reassess promptly if the price invalidates the setup; the greater the volatility, the more restrained each position size should be. 美财政部加码制裁切断伊朗金融通道，美元走强，风险资产承压。

美国财政部对伊朗实施新一轮金融制裁，目标是把伊朗彻底隔离在全球美元体系之外。消息落地后美元指数应声反弹。制裁本身不直接涉及加密市场，但传导路径很直接：地缘紧张升温 + 美元走强，双杀风险资产。

对市场的影响
- 短期：美元反弹意味着全球资金涌向避险资产，BTC这类风险资产被抽血。传导链是：美元涨 → 风险偏好下降 → 加密市场资金流出 → BTC承压。目前BTC在$78,948.06、24h仅+1.50%，ETH $2,484.74，涨幅都偏弱，说明买盘已经在犹豫。XRP这类和美元流动性预期绑得更紧的资产，24h已经-3.23%先跌为敬。
- 中期：制裁加深伊朗经济孤立，区域市场动荡可能持续发酵。同时全球对美元依赖反而增强，这对加密的“去美元化叙事”是阶段性打击。

我的判断
我短期看空。地缘冲突类消息历史上对BTC是利空，叠加美元走强，12小时内$78,948.06这个位置大概率守不住，下方关注$77,500支撑。ETH $2,484.74相对更弱，24h只涨0.45%，如果BTC回落，ETH跌得会更狠。反转信号只有两个：美元回吐涨幅，或者地缘消息没有后续升级。在那之前，别急着接飞刀。

Crypto options implied volatility has surged. Markets like Deribit are pricing in that BTC, ETH, XRP, and SOL will see large price swings before August 30. Everyone’s risk controls need to be recalculated.

Deribit’s latest options data hasn’t been calm. The implied volatility for XRP, SOL, ETH, and BTC in contracts expiring on August 30 has clearly risen, suggesting that option sellers are demanding a higher risk premium. In plain terms, professional traders are willing to pay more for protection because they believe the probability of a big move in the next two weeks is increasing. This kind of signal often comes ahead of the spot market—before several major volatility events in 2024, a similar structure showed up.

Note that rising volatility doesn’t determine direction; both up and down count.

Market impact
- Short term: Market makers will widen bid-ask spreads accordingly, and leveraged players’ funding rates as well as the distance to liquidation will all need to be re-calculated. BTC is currently at $79,036.01, ETH at $2,483.04—the volatility range implied by the options market suggests swings will be much larger than the recent realized move.
- Medium term: As the August 30 expiry approaches, the Gamma effect may amplify price oscillations, and near the Wall it’s easy to see wick-like pin actions. On the institutional side, hedging ratios may be increased, and spot sell pressure and buy pressure will both be amplified.

My take
Slightly neutral with a wait-and-see stance. Rising implied volatility only tells you “something is coming,” not which way it will go—so at this point, betting on direction has a low edge.

For BTC: if it breaks below the $79,036.01 support level, volatility may release to the downside; if it holds above $79,036.01, it leans upward. The foundation of DeFi. The home of NFTs. A pioneer of smart contracts.

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation If you peel back Dusk’s marketing shell and get straight to the code layer, its architecture actually hides quite a few tricks. First, look at the “card” (the deciding factors) behind the SA (Succinct Attestation) protocol: the system directly locks each round’s consensus voting seats to 64. That means no matter how many nodes are just idling online, the only participants that can truly take the seats to make decisions are always those 64 slots. Also, the commonly said claim that “67 nodes are equivalent to Algorand’s security” is complete nonsense. In the source code, the “0.67” clearly means that among those 64 people, block production requires the approval ratio to reach 67%—yet many people have twisted it into a supposed network-wide node threshold.

Next, consider its ledger. This tokenomics setup is basically a grinder for retail users. As long as a node wins the block packaging right, it can immediately pocket 70% of the base rewards plus up to an additional 10% in tips. After the development team siphons off 10%, the remaining 10% is split between two small groups. What does that mean? If your capital is small and you don’t have the “lucky charm” to get selected as a “main node,” then relying only on those meager participation fees may not even cover the electricity cost for cloud servers.

This kind of extremely skewed incentive network inevitably leads to capital consolidating into a tight circle. Right now, 206 Provisioners are running on the mainnet, with a total of 218 million DUSK locked in the pool. On the surface, it looks pretty thriving—but when you cut open the picture and look at the distribution: the top 20 giants directly control more than 35% of the share. In the world of PoS, the size of your stake equals the probability of producing blocks. When big capital aggressively feeds on rewards and then reinvests (rolls the stake) again, it doesn’t just crush small retail participants—it also forms an ever-growing power black hole.

Finally, and most fatally: the machines’ real-world locations are completely hidden. Whether you dig through official materials or consult an on-chain explorer, you can’t find the physical geographic ownership of these machines at all. If most of these hundreds of servers end up concentrated in a single AWS availability zone, and that datacenter loses connectivity, the entire chain will have to stall. So the conclusion is very straightforward: as long as you don’t publish the two key pieces—(1) the Gini coefficient of the token distribution and (2) the geographical topology structure—Dusk’s so-called “anti-censorship” and “decentralization” is just empty talk. #eth $ETH

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation Sitting idle, I’ve been browsing the codebase of @Dusk_Foundation  for a while, and a particular setting jumps out at me so clearly that it has me thinking hard: FIRST_REDUCTION_COMMITTEE_SIZE: usize = 64. In short, no matter how much the ecosystem might grow in the future, the seats that determine block results—those seats are forever locked to 64. Dusk is indeed aiming at real-world assets (RWA) and compliant finance, and it can finalize an accounting entry in 15 seconds, with speed that’s truly top-tier. But with only these 64 spots, was this an unfortunate move by the dev team made to accelerate development, or has the “decentralization” DNA of this whole system been capped from the very beginning?

Following this thread, its allocation model looks even more glaring. If you look up the latest audit materials, you can see that each new block currently releases 19.86 DUSK. Here’s how it’s divided: the winner who grabs the right to record the ledger takes 70% of the base subsidy straight away, and with performance included, they can capture up to 80% of the block’s profit. And what about the leftovers? Two scoring teams each get 5%, and the development treasury keeps 10%. That effectively stuffs the lion’s share into the hands of a very small number of people. Meanwhile, those retail node operators who only sometimes hit the lottery have to shoulder the exact same machine maintenance costs—there’s simply not much room to survive.

When all the chips are concentrated among the large holders, it’s also a hurdle that can’t really be avoided. On-chain data can’t lie: currently, more than 207 million DUSK are tied up in active accounts. And among roughly 200 work nodes, the top 20 big players already hold more than 35% of the chips; the top five giants alone control over 60% of the circulating supply. On the surface, they say it’s blind selection based on cryptography, but given the sheer scale of capital at this crushing level, big players are simply using money to buy high-probability outcomes.

Finally, there’s one more information blind spot: where exactly are these machines located? The whitepaper only says how the hardware should be configured, but says nothing about the physical locations of these servers. The claim circulating in the community—“67 nodes can reach Algorand-level security strength”—can’t be found with solid evidence in the official documentation either. With the banner of a compliant chain, this 64-person inner circle, the heavy skew of 19.86 rewarded per block, and the fact that tokens are banded together—everything points to the fact that people should scrutinize these vulnerabilities with a magnifying glass.

Has anyone noticed these details? Is this truly pragmatic technical compromise, or is it simply impossible to cross the decentralization threshold in the first place?#eth $ETH

BTC gains close to 3%, open interest increases only mildly: so who’s buying this time?

$BTC is up nearly 3% over the past 24 hours, while open interest has only risen moderately. So who’s buying here—and why hasn’t the derivatives market pushed the rally even hotter?

Fact: On Binance USD-perpetual contracts, $BTC is at $79,764, up 2.91% in 24 hours, with trading volume of about $18.75 billion; $ETH is at $2,490, up 1.32%, with volume of about $14.83 billion. BTC and ETH are both TRADING.

But over the last three hours, the notional value of BTC open positions has only increased by about 0.74%, and ETH by about 0.72%. BTC funding rate is around 0.59 bps, and it hasn’t clearly heated up along with the near-3% intraday gain. Price expansion is happening faster than the growth in new positions—this isn’t the same as “a surge driven by a pile of leverage chasing price.”

Funding reality: According to Farside’s latest data, on August 24, U.S. spot BTC ETF net inflows were $125.4 million, and ETH ETF net inflows were $20.2 million. This suggests spot demand is still present, but it doesn’t prove that every minute of this move is ETF buying—and it can’t rule out short-covering by shorts or short-term spot-driven momentum.

Why can positive factors and price reaction be inconsistent? Because ETFs reflect the allocation results from the previous trading day, while perpetual contracts trade today’s risk appetite. If price rises while open interest increases only modestly, it could mean spot moved first—or that shorts are being forced out.

The market is still confirming: after the rise, can trades continue and pullbacks get absorbed, instead of judging everything from a single bullish candle.

For longs to be “right,” BTC needs to hold steady and keep trading active, with open interest increasing moderately and funding remaining restrained—that would indicate the new risk hasn’t run out of control. For shorts to be “right,” price rises then falls back, with open interest accelerating again while trading volume can’t keep up—that would imply that chasing leverage is taking over. The most common mistake is to treat a low fee rate as if there’s no risk.

My view: I’m more inclined to watch whether, during BTC’s pullback, there’s still spot absorption—then use that to judge whether this rally can continue. A rally without being overcrowded is a good sign, but it’s not a guarantee against a drop. Without volume support, a breakout can quickly turn into two-way liquidations. Risk warning: near round-number support/resistance levels, both liquidity and liquidations can amplify volatility—keep position sizes light and pre-set stop-losses.

Both Encrypted IRA Platforms Were Hacked at the Same Time—And the Attacker Is Still the Same Person: Are Retail Investors’ Retirement Funds Safe?

Bitcoin IRA and iTrustCapital suffered data breaches by the same attacker, exposing users’ personal and account information security.

These two platforms, which mainly promote “buying crypto with retirement accounts,” disclosed data breaches one after another. Security researchers linked the two incidents to the same threat actor—Tiffanny Milanovich. These IRA platforms manage retail investors’ long-term retirement money, and the leaked data includes users’ personal information and account details. The exact scale of the breach and the monetary losses have not been fully disclosed by either platform, and that in itself is a problem.

Impact on the market
- Short term: Limited impact on BTC and ETH spot prices. At the moment, BTC is $78,772.01 (24h +1.80%) and the trend is stable. What’s truly affected is users’ confidence in the platforms—having your retirement account hacked is more alarming than losing money trading crypto, and it could trigger a new wave of withdrawals.
- Medium term: Events like this give the SEC and the Department of Labor more reasons to tighten scrutiny of crypto IRA platforms. Custodial security and information-disclosure requirements are likely to be upgraded, and compliance costs for smaller platforms will be pushed higher.

My take
To be honest, this kind of security incident has weak transmission to the broader market—BTC will rise if it’s going to rise. But it’s an ongoing structural risk reminder: the security level of the coins you keep on a platform depends on the platform’s weakest link. On the spot-price side, I maintain a neutral-to-bullish view. BTC has held above $78,772, and SOL is up 5.60%, so sentiment hasn’t been completely derailed. What to watch is whether subsequent disclosures escalate—if private keys or custodial assets are involved, the situation changes entirely, and that would be a truly bearish development. For now, treat this as an information-leak issue and monitor the follow-up notices.

85% of fake-coin (altcoin) funding rates exceed the average; last time this happened was at the BTC historical top: is the altseason signal still an overheat warning?

Glassnode data: 85% of altcoin funding rates are higher than their own averages, reaching a new high since the last BTC all-time high. Leverage sentiment is clearly heating up.

Glassnode’s latest report shows the altcoin market has entered an optimistic phase—85% of altcoin perpetual contracts’ funding rates are above their respective historical averages. This proportion is the highest level since the previous BTC all-time high. Funding rates are the periodic payments between long and short positions; persistently elevated rates mean longs are willing to hold at higher costs. Glassnode specifically notes that in the altcoin market, this funding-rate condition can last for weeks and does not immediately revert to the mean.

Impact on the market
- Short term: Altcoin sentiment is overheated, but a pullback may not happen right away. SOL is up 4.6% today to $99.33, BTC is stabilizing near $79,013.99, and XRP is actually down 1.71% to $1.485—internally within the sector there is already divergence. In a high funding-rate environment, once BTC sells off with volume, the cascade of altcoin liquidations would be even more severe.
- Medium term: If funding rates remain elevated for several weeks, it usually corresponds to the continuation period of the altcoin “catch-up” rally, but it also reflects a process of capital gradually shifting from “smart money” to leveraged retail traders.

My take
My view: the data is bullish, but the positioning is risky. BTC holding above $79,013.99 suggests the main uptrend structure hasn’t broken. High funding rates for altcoins in the early-to-middle stage of the rally are a confirmation signal; in the late stage, it can be a sign of a harvest. Right now it’s in between—what matters is whether BTC can hold the $77,500 area. If it does, altcoins still have room to catch up further; if it breaks down, the pullback for high funding-rate altcoins will be much harsher than the broader market. Chasing leverage at this moment is the worst setup—waiting for the funding rate to cool before reassessing is safer.

Central Banks Worldwide Publicly Express Concern Over a USD Stablecoin Threat to Monetary Sovereignty

Multiple central banks warn that USD stablecoins are eroding domestic monetary policy. In the short term, this is sentiment-positive for BTC/ETH.

According to Crypto Briefing, central bank officials collectively spoke out: the expansion of USD stablecoins is threatening their monetary sovereignty. Put simply, the more widely dollar-pegged stablecoins such as USDT and USDC circulate globally (especially in emerging markets), the more people effectively end up holding dollars. This then sidelines local-currency deposits and interest-rate policy adjustments. When central banks raise rates to fight inflation, people turn around and buy stablecoins—making policy directly ineffective.

Market impact
- Short term: In essence, this news is another official endorsement of stablecoin status—if even central banks admit it has grown large enough to threaten sovereignty. This is sentiment-positive for BTC $77,687.99 and ETH $2,461.22, and the market is green today as well (XRP 24h +3.51%). However, the impact level is limited; it won’t directly trigger a major breakout.
- Medium term: Two possible paths—either countries accelerate the rollout of their own CBDCs to counter it, or they tighten regulation of USD stablecoins. In emerging markets (high-inflation countries like Turkey, Nigeria, and Argentina), stablecoin demand will be even more rigid. Ultimately, a substantial portion of this capital will flow into BTC.

My view
My stance: neutral to bullish. Central banks claim it threatens sovereignty, but none of them can produce an effective block-off solution, so dollar stablecoin penetration will continue. If BTC holds the $75K level, the trend remains intact; above that, we’ll see whether it can hold firm at $80K. For ETH, there is support around $2,400. The real risk isn’t this news, but a certain country suddenly rolling out a hard ban policy, which would trigger short-term risk-avoidance selling pressure.

One-sentence translation: Central banks oppose it, which only proves that the stablecoin pipeline can’t be shut down—and the end of the pipeline often leads to BTC.

title: 早上打开电脑，最该先处理的不是行情，是本周会确定花掉的钱
subTitle:
早上打开电脑，最该先处理的不是行情，是本周会确定花掉的钱

很多加密用户早上第一件事是看 BTC、看 ETH、看昨晚有没有异动。但真正影响一天效率的，往往不是仓位多涨了 1%，而是 AI 会员到期、代码工具续不上、购物卡还没准备好、团队采购临时要付款。

这类钱有一个共同点：它不再是“也许要花”的预算，而是已经确定会发生的支出。既然确定要花，就不该继续被放在交易路径里等临时处理。

最容易被低估的是时间成本。你以为只是从链上资产到一次付款，中间却可能多出好几步：换资产、等到账、补支付方式、确认能不能扣款、失败后再找备用路径。金额越小，越不值得把它做成一套临时工程。

AI 订阅尤其明显。一个月几十美元的会员费，看起来不大，但如果它卡在工作开始前，损失的不是手续费，而是今天的写作、编程、客服、设计、数据处理全部被打断。生产力工具的账单，应该像水电费一样提前处理，而不是到期那一刻才想办法。

礼品卡也是同样的逻辑。很多购物、订阅和日常采购，本质上已经有明确预算。与其等到结账页再研究怎么把加密资产变成可用余额，不如早上先把未来几天会花的钱拆出来，让它直接进入能消费的状态。

反常识一点说，成熟的资金管理不是只会盯收益率，而是知道哪部分钱还可以承担波动，哪部分钱今天就要变成购买力。仓位归仓位，生活预算归生活预算，二者混在一起，最后经常不是赚少了，而是该花的时候花不出去。

translatedData.subTitle:
When you open your computer in the morning, the first thing you should handle isn’t market news—it’s the money that will definitely be spent this week.

For many crypto users, the first thing they do in the morning is check BTC, check ETH, and see whether anything moved overnight. But what truly affects a day’s efficiency is often not whether your position gained 1%, but whether your AI membership expires, whether your code tools can’t be renewed, whether your shopping card isn’t ready yet, or whether the team’s procurement suddenly needs payment.

This kind of money has one thing in common: it’s no longer a budget for “maybe we’ll spend it,” but an expense that’s already guaranteed to happen. Since it’s certain, it shouldn’t keep sitting on the transaction pipeline waiting for temporary handling.

33.91%! TAC totally blew my mind. In the first hour after opening, it directly surged to 0.002278—it's only a tiny bit away from the 24h high. Honestly, I didn’t expect it to be this strong. But even weirder is that it was a volume-backed pump—1.4x the average volume. That’s got something.

First, let’s talk about the overall market. BTC and ETH have both been climbing steadily this week. BTC is up 22.5% over 7 days, and ETH is even more outrageous—up 30%. The Fear & Greed Index is hovering right at 50, right at the neutral zone. The market is neither euphoric nor panicked. In this kind of environment, funds are basically playing selectively—not blindly rushing in.

Alright, honestly, the top three gainers today—TAC, PROM, and UAI—each has its own storyline. I’ll break them down one by one.

**TAC, current price 0.0023, is already hugging the 24h high of 0.002278—less than 1% away.** This position is the most awkward: chase it and risk standing guard at a high level; don’t chase and worry it’ll keep running. My approach is: if you already hold some, don’t rush to exit. See whether it can break out of the resistance at 0.002278 with volume. If it breaks and holds, the upside space opens up. If it fails, consider buying back around 0.0020. 
For a bullish reference range: entry 0.0021–0.00215, stop loss 0.00195 (if it drops back below support from about the last 8 candles, then you’re wrong and should admit it), first target 0.0025. The risk-reward works out to about 1:2.5—not bad.
**Invalidation condition: if it drops below 0.00177 on heavy volume and can’t reclaim it, then this pump is basically over—don’t keep fighting it.**

Next is PROM. I’m a bit conflicted here. It’s up 26.17%, but the volume is shrinking—only 0.6x the average volume.
**What does a low-volume surge mean?** It means sell pressure isn’t heavy, but it also suggests the chasing capital isn’t that decisive. 
Now it’s at 3.63, with about 10% room until the 24h high at 4.055, but the resistance from the past ~8 candles is at 3.841. The funding rate is 0.005%, which is normal—no overheating signal. My take: short-term bullish, but don’t get greedy. Reference range: entry 3.55–3.60, stop loss 3.45 (if it breaks below the rebound trendline of the 24h low at 2.6), first target 3.84, RR roughly around 1:1.5. If you want a better risk-reward, you can wait for a pullback to around 3.50 to enter then—the RR can reach about 1:2.5.
**Invalidation condition: if price falls below 3.45 and volume expands to 1.5x the average volume or more, it suggests someone is distributing/selling.**

Finally UAI. This coin’s funding rate is 0.0985%, already in a long-side overheating state.
**A funding rate that high means longs are crowded in the futures market.** This is when the most common scenario is an “impaler pin” move—first squeeze the shorts, then crush the longs. 
It’s currently 0.3518; the 24h high is 0.3878. The current price is around the 77% position within the range, but volume is only about 0.3x the average volume—that signal isn’t great. Personally, I’m cautious on UAI for the short term. If you absolutely want to participate, I suggest waiting for a pullback near the 0.3452 support level. If it breaks 0.34, then completely give up. **Don’t chase at these extremely high funding-rate levels.** Last time I did exactly that, and I took a big loss (yeah, saying more is just more tears).

By the way, let me mention the biggest losers list: VELVET -76.65%, TUT -25.69%, STORJ funding rate -0.6656%—shorts overheated but the price is still falling… stay away from coins like this. Seriously, don’t touch them.

My overall stance: Fear & Greed Index at 50 is neutral, the broader market is stable, but the altcoin market is highly differentiated.
**In this kind of market, the best thing to do is: pick the right direction, control your position size, don’t chase highs, and wait for a pullback.** For short-term ideas, follow the ranges I gave above. For the mid-term, I actually like projects like PROM with real ZK technical background—pullbacks are opportunities.

Oh, one more thing—are you guys watching ZANO? It’s on the trending list. It didn’t make it into the gainers today, but coins that are “trending yet not moving” often are just building a big move… or maybe I’m just sour again (manual doge head).

Chat in the comments—what did you catch today? As for me, I watched TAC rise from 0.0015 all the way up… and still missed the entry. Damn.

然后是PROM，这个我有点纠结。涨幅26.17%但缩量了，只有均量的0.6倍。**缩量上涨意味着什么？意味着卖盘不重，但也说明追涨的资金不够坚决。** 现在3.63，距离24h高点4.055还有10%的空间，但近8根K线的阻力在3.841。资金费率0.005%正常，没有过热信号。我的判断是：短线偏多但别贪，参考区间入场3.55-3.60，止损3.45（跌破24h低点2.6的反弹趋势线），第一目标3.84，RR大概1:1.5左右。如果你想要更高的盈亏比，可以等它回踩3.50附近再上，那时候RR能到1:2.5。**失效条件：如果价格跌破3.45且成交量放大到均量1.5倍以上，说明有人在出货。**

最后说UAI，这个币的资金费率0.0985%，已经是多头过热的状态了。**费率过高意味着合约市场上看多的人太拥挤，这时候最容易出现"插针"行情——先拉爆空头，再杀多头。** 现在0.3518，24h高点0.3878，当前价处于区间77%的位置，但缩量只有0.3倍均量，这个信号不太好。我个人对UAI短线偏谨慎，如果非要参与，建议等回调到0.3452支撑位附近再看，跌破0.34就彻底放弃。**别在费率这么高的时候追高，上次我就是这么吃了个大亏（是的，说多了都是泪）。**

顺便提一嘴跌幅榜，VELVET -76.65%，TUT -25.69%，STORJ资金费率-0.6656%空头过热但价格还在跌……这种币别碰，真别碰。

我的整体态度：恐惧贪婪指数50中性，大盘稳但山寨分化严重。**这种行情最适合做的事：选对方向，控制仓位，别追高，等回调。** 短线思路就按我上面给的区间来，中线的话我更看好PROM这种有实际ZK技术背景的项目，回调就是机会。

对了，你们有没有在盯ZANO？热搜榜上挂着呢，虽然今天没进涨幅榜，但这种"热搜但没动静"的币往往是在憋大招……也可能是我又酸了（手动狗头）。

评论区聊聊，你们今天抓到哪个了？我反正是看着TAC从0.0015一路涨上来的，又踏空了，妈的。

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  Observing @Dusk_Foundation  for longer, I’m just not impressed by those technically polished “soft articles” anymore. Now all that’s left in my head is a soul-piercing question: with this underlying network being hyped to the skies and beyond, can it actually bring DUSK real, hard-earned money for us?

Looking back to August 15th, the official was still working hard to promote the on-chain tokenization of private equity for small and medium-sized enterprises, laying out the entire process—asset verification, transfer, and dividend distribution—as if every step were crystal clear. This track does indeed sound more solid than fictional RWA. But as a token holder, I’m still completely in the dark: even if real companies truly come to issue assets, through what channel does the commercial value they generate flow into the pockets of retail investors like us?

In the end, at this stage, the real purpose of $DUSK  is nothing more than paying Gas fees and staking/locking up. Let’s look at this lethal token distribution: total supply is capped at 1 billion tokens; the first batch released is 500 million, and the remaining 500 million is planned to trickle toward the market over 36 years. What’s terrifying is that just in the first four years, about 250.48 million tokens need to be minted. Right now, node profits are entirely pinned on “system payroll plus on-chain revenue share,” and no matter what, the development team is still guaranteed to take 10% of the dividends unchanged.

This kind of high-inflation play is definitely a minefield you don’t dare to dig into. If the chain is bustling every day, and the constant wave of transactions and interactions consumes all the newly minted tokens, then sure—this looks great. But if the ecosystem turns into a dead pond, then nodes have to rely on the system minting out of thin air just to generate rewards. Isn’t that essentially mortgaging tomorrow’s dump of token supply to artificially keep the network stable and alive today?

The team is still up early and busy upgrading that Boreas, with the codebase changing so fast it’s dizzying. But I’m not really interested in any of that anymore. I just want the most direct business scorecard: how many real, live projects have actually gone live on the mainnet? Every month, exactly how many fees can be burned? Do these concrete inflows sufficiently offset the brand-new token supply the system pumps out every day?

You can keep pounding the code blindly, but in the token’s ledger, it’s always a close-quarters brawl between inflation and deflation.

I’ve never doubted their engineering prowess. I’m just waiting—dead set—for Dusk to break through: to have the true on-chain consumption rate thoroughly crush that astonishing token emission rate. #eth $ETH

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation 观察 @Dusk_Foundation 越久，我越对那些包装精美的技术软文提不起劲。现在脑子里只剩下一个直击灵魂的拷问：这套底层网络吹得上天入地，到底能不能给咱们 DUSK 带来护盘的真金白银？

回顾 8 月 15 日，官方还在卖力宣传中小企业私募股权上链，把确权、流转和派息的全流程讲得头头是道。这赛道确实比虚构的 RWA 听着踏实。但作为持币者我依旧一头雾水：就算实体公司真跑来发行资产了，他们产生的商业价值，究竟通过什么管道流进咱们散户的口袋里？

说到底，现阶段 $DUSK 的真正用处无非就是付 Gas 费和质押锁仓。咱们看看这要命的筹码分布：总量封顶 10 亿枚，首批投放了 5 亿，剩下的 5 亿计划用 36 年慢慢流向市场。让人头皮发麻的是，仅仅前 4 年就要砸出约 2.5048 亿枚。眼下节点的利润全指望“系统发工资加链上抽成”硬顶着，而且不管怎么分，开发团队还要雷打不动地拿走 10% 的分红。

这种高通胀的玩法，绝对是不敢深究的雷区。假如链上天天车水马龙，靠海量的交互消耗把新产出的代币统统抵消，那当然是好事；可一旦生态成了一滩死水，节点全靠系统无中生有地造币来发奖励，这不就等于透支明天的砸盘筹码，来为今天的网络稳定强行续命吗？

眼看团队还在起早贪黑地折腾那个 Boreas 升级，代码库更新得眼花缭乱。但我现在真不关心这些，只想看最直接的商业成绩单：主网到底落地了几个活着的项目？每个月究竟能销毁多少手续费？这些实打实的进账，够不够对冲系统每天疯狂涌出的新筹码？

代码可以蒙着头一直敲，但在代币的账本里，永远只有通胀与通缩的贴身肉搏。

我从来没怀疑过这帮人的研发手腕，我只是在死死等着 Dusk 破局：让真实的链上消耗速度，彻彻底底地碾压它那惊人的增发率。#eth $ETH

Overnight, US stocks fell, while US Treasury yields added to the “devaluation trade” sentiment. Overall, risk assets came under pressure and crypto prices followed lower.

Bloomberg Television’s latest Wall Street closing show invited a line-up of heavyweight guests: Bill Quigley, co-founder of Tether and CEO of Principal Asset Management; a software industry analyst from Goldman Sachs; Torsten Slok, Chief Economist at Apollo; and others. The discussion centered on three areas: weakness in the AI sector represented by Nvidia; elevated US Treasury yields; and the so-called “currency devaluation trade” — investors rushing into hard assets like gold and Bitcoin due to concerns about fiat purchasing power shrinking.

At the day’s close, US stocks slid and BTC was $78,920.01 (24h -1.75%), ETH was $2,482.03 (-1.03%), and XRP fell the most to $1.48 (-2.88%).

Market impact
- Short term: When US stock technology shares (especially AI-related names) weaken, it has historically weighed on crypto risk appetite. BTC’s -1.75% essentially tracked the Nasdaq’s rhythm. If yields don’t come down, leveraged funds won’t move. But watch the counter-logic: if the “devaluation trade” narrative really takes hold, it could actually be bullish for BTC in the medium to long term.
- Medium term: When Tether co-founder appeared on mainstream financial programs to discuss this topic, it showed that crypto narratives have entered the Wall Street mainstream agenda. Macro views from traditional institutions like Apollo could indirectly influence how capital allocates toward BTC.

My view
Slightly bearish in the short term. BTC around the $78,920 area faces near-term pressure. Below, focus on support around $78,920.01. If the US stock AI sector continues to adjust, the probability of a pullback isn’t low. However, this drop is driven by macro liquidity, not something going wrong specifically in crypto. The deeper the sell-off, the more it could provide an “entry narrative” for “devaluation trade” capital. ETH is relatively resilient (-1.03%), and within weakness it looks comparatively healthy. XRP’s -2.88% requires caution for a follow-through drop. Strategy-wise, it’s mainly a wait-and-see approach, looking for a turning point in yields or signs that US stocks stabilize.

In the past three hours, the spot order book has seen twelve consecutive net inflows. Over the past week, the ETF has added another 280,000 units, and Bitmine has turned around to pick up another 32,000—big money is buying this aggressively, yet the price is still stuck near the seven-day high and grinding along just below it. This rhythm is pretty interesting.

I only understood the details after going through the contract terms: the funding rate is still down on the floor at 0.01%, and the basis is hovering right around zero. After a full week of gains—starting at least from 30 points—you’d expect some kind of leveraged frenzy, but there hasn’t been one. This rally is all spot real-money buying; not even a spark of fuel from retail chasing highs.

Look at positioning: large holders have 65% of their real positions standing long, while retail is calling for longs at 70%—retail is even more daring than the big players, but the big players haven’t left, which means they haven’t left. Net inflows of 520,000 units over three hours provide the foundation—real gold and silver.

I’m standing long. RSI hitting 79 really is hot and heavy, so it’s normal that short-term moves get pressed while grinding. But since real money hasn’t pulled out and leverage isn’t heating up, the structure hasn’t broken. The day the spot order book flips to consecutive net outflows, or the price breaks through and falls below the 20-line—that’s when real money is running. At that point, the longs are invalid. Until then, don’t let go of your long positions.

ETH jumps 30% in a week—Gemini Vault company keeps疯狂 snapping up
Ethereum has gone absolutely wild this week, surging 30% week-over-week and posting its strongest performance since May last year. It has already broken directly through the $2,500 mark.
Even more dramatic is Bitmine, a crypto vault firm. Last week it added another 32,447 ETH, worth roughly $81 million. This is the largest single-week buy since early July. In the words of the boss, Tom Lee: a 30% weekly gain might just be the prelude to a bigger move. Even their own company is casting a vote with action—this is more convincing than any research report.
Why is it so strong? First, US Treasury buybacks have lit up the whole risk-asset complex. Second, the ETH ecosystem really is bouncing back: staking yields are steady, on-chain activity is lively, and vault companies are buying like crazy—one after another. More importantly, the ETH/BTC exchange rate hasn’t been this strong in a long time. Clearly, capital is rotating toward Ethereum. This suggests the move isn’t just chasing the market—it’s an independent trend.
On-chain data shows whale addresses are increasing their ETH holdings, while exchange ETH balances are actually declining. That means more people are buying and fewer are selling. This supply-demand structure, historically, often corresponds to a solid, meaningful run in the market. On top of that, the Ethereum ETF side has also started delivering ongoing net inflows. From an institutional standpoint, they’re also stepping up. Retail investors are still hesitating, but the “smart money” has already moved.
Beyond the secondary market, the staking track is heating up too—locked-up volume keeps climbing, and the entire ecosystem feels like someone has pressed the acceleration button.
My view: corporate crypto treasuries are shifting from a Bitcoin-only solo act to a two-main-roles story. More and more companies are treating ETH as a reserve asset, which is completely different from the old thinking of only recognizing “big BTC.”
But a reminder: if it rises too fast, a pullback is likely. Don’t chase at the top—buy in batches. The trend is something you build by moving, not something you simply call out. Only those who can hold deserve this round of momentum.

وقال قاليباف: "يعلم الأمريكيون أن لا أحد يصدق تهديداتهم. اقتصاديًا، لا تستطيع الولايات المتحدة فرض المزيد من القيود على علاقاتها مع الدول الأخرى". 
وبالتالى نحن نجد أنفسنا الضحيه ومن سيقوم بمراقبة الاسعار خاصه أننا نعيش في هذه الفتره مثل الماكينات لا نتوقف عن العمل

Originally BTC touched exactly 80,000.

But then ETH fell back to 2,475.

BTC itself also dropped back to 78,749.

First, let’s talk about volume.

BTC’s trading value is 2.369 billion (not an explosion in volume).

All the volume is stacked in that half-hour as it surged toward 80,000.

After that, it keeps getting less and less.

This is profit-taking exiting—not panic selling rushing out.

The problem is stuck at 80,000.

This is where the 24-hour high is, and the Bollinger upper band is also here.

MA5 is at 78,200, and MA20 is at 77,500.

Price is holding above those levels.

RSI is 58.

MACD has a golden cross; the histogram is at 48.5, but it’s shorter than yesterday by a bit.

The bullish momentum has shed half its strength.

At the open, it’ll likely pull back first to around 78,200.

Once it holds, then we try again at 80,000.

Chasing longs from this level isn’t meaningful.

ETH is only up 0.85%, clearly weaker than BTC.

RSI is just 52, and the MACD histogram has only just flipped positive to 3.8.

2,533 is the previous high, and 2,437 is MA20.

Without volume, BTC can’t move; and without that, ETH can’t rise.

I’m planning to have BTC pull back to 78,200 and place a buy order there.

Stop loss at 77,400; target 79,800—take half off first.

The premise is: during the pullback, it doesn’t come with heavy volume that breaks through 77,800.

If it directly breaks down with volume, I’ll cancel this trade.

But everyone’s cost basis is different.

At the same level, some people dare to catch while others need to run—tell me, isn’t that the truth?

The August market is grinding all the way to the end of the month.

• BTC $79,155 (+2.57%): 1D RSI14 at 86.3 extremely overbought. MACD longs expanded with increased volume—riding the upper Bollinger Band is strong but stretched. 4H RSI 73.6 “fast” golden cross, bandwidth narrowed to 3.48%. 1H RSI 62.7 healthy.
• ETH $2,486 (+1.88%): 1D RSI14 at 88.4, the most overbought across the board—stronger than BTC.
• SOL $96.65 (+1.3%): also rising; 4H/1H are the weakest.
📌 Daily/weekly are extremely overbought and digesting the squeeze. 4H/1H momentum is back to neutral; thin volume over the weekend and Bollinger Band tightening at  
→ direction is yet to be chosen.

⚙️ Derivatives
• Funding rates: exchanges collectively +0.01%/8h mild positive (shorts paying, not at extreme values).
• Spot premium: -0.009% / -$7 (no premium buy demand). “Fear & Greed” at 73 (Greed).
• Volume is up across the board, but it’s more like a squeeze impulse rather than healthy absorption—watch for pin risk over the weekend.

📉 U.S. Stocks (midday): Memory crash—Micron -5.9%, SanDisk/WD -7.7%, Hynix -7.6% (profit-taking ahead of NVDA earnings); Nasdaq QQQ -0.9%; crypto-related stocks MSTR +2.1% / BMNR +4.9% (red vs. the market).

🧭 Overall View
The bigger structure bull trend hasn’t broken, and the devaluation trade theme is still intact. The current short-term extreme overbought looks “strong but stretched,” not a clear top. $79,999 is the nearest resistance—only after it holds steady should new upside open up. • SOL: Resistance $95–96; support $92. Weakest among the bunch.
• Discipline: With overbought conditions + an event-heavy week, don’t max out position size and don’t chase vertical moves—wait for 1H confirmation and a wider stop.

Back in the 94 wave of 2017, I’ve seen similar situations. Big institutions don’t say anything publicly, but the fund flows behind the scenes tell the whole story. Now Tom Lee’s Bitmine has scooped up 81 million ETH in a single week—that’s the largest weekly buy since July.

History won’t simply repeat itself, but human nature has always been the same.

The ETH/BTC golden cross is also worth a closer look. Don’t just stare at the words “bullish”—what I care about is what’s behind them: capital isn’t merely trading concepts, it’s positioning around improvements in ETH’s fundamentals. L2, ecosystem upgrades, the RWA narrative… these are slowly moving from slide decks to real settlement.

But what I really want to say today isn’t these good pieces of news.

Term Finance was hacked for 8.5 million—its attack method is quite interesting: not a contract vulnerability, but a governance vulnerability. With relatively little money to buy voting power, attackers can steer protocol decisions. This exposes an issue many people overlook: the “decentralization” of many DeFi protocols is mostly surface-level; governance tokens are highly concentrated, and the number of participants who truly vote is pitifully small.

What does this mean in practical terms?

First, protocols where governance tokens are highly dispersed and voting participation rates are low will become future targets for attackers. Second, for the Ethereum ecosystem to genuinely move toward compliant asset management, governance security is a must-have lesson to make up—this isn’t a technical problem, it’s a business logic problem. Whoever can help these protocols strengthen governance will have the opportunity.

I’ll say it again: while others discuss concepts, I’m thinking about whether they can be implemented. This round of ETH’s 30% weekly surge isn’t driven by hype—it’s double confirmation by both capital and logic. But don’t chase it; wait for a pullback to see whether it can hold at 2377—that’s when the real test comes.

2017年94那波，我见过类似的情形。大机构明面上不说话，但私底下资金流动说明一切。现在Tom Lee的Bitmine一周扫了8100万ETH——这是7月以来最大的单周买入量。

历史不会简单重复，但人性从来一样。

ETH/BTC的黄金交叉也值得细看。别光盯着"看涨"两个字，我更在意的是背后意味着什么：资金不只是在炒概念，而是在布局ETH的基本面改善。L2、生态升级、RWA叙事……这些慢慢从PPT走向了真实结算。

但我今天真正想说的不是这些好消息。

Term Finance被黑850万，攻击手法很有意思——不是合约漏洞，是治理漏洞。花不多的钱买投票权，就能操控协议决策。这暴露了一个很多人忽视的问题：很多DeFi协议的"去中心化"只是表面文章，治理代币高度集中，真正投票的少得可怜。

这件事落到实处意味着什么？

第一，那些治理代币高度分散、投票参与率低的协议，未来会成攻击者的靶子。第二，以太坊生态要真正走向合规资管，治理安全是必须补的课——这不是技术问题，是商业逻辑问题。谁能帮这些协议加固治理，谁就有机会。

我还是那句话：别人讨论概念，我讨论能不能落地。ETH这波30%的周涨幅，背后不是情绪，是资金和逻辑的双重确认。但也别追，等回踩2377看能不能守住，那时候才是真正考验。

这波ETH的治理问题，你觉得未来会倒逼出什么样的解决方案？

JPMorgan leads a letter to FinCEN, urging that the stablecoin secondary market be brought under KYC

💡 Slightly bearish / more negative than neutral: expectations of tighter regulation may suppress sentiment in the short term

A U.S. big-bank lobbying group has advised FinCEN to expand KYC rules to the stablecoin secondary market, directly targeting exchanges.

What’s going on?
The Bank Policy Institute (BPI)—whose members include Wall Street giants such as JPMorgan, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, and Citigroup—has just submitted recommendations to the U.S. Treasury’s FinCEN: extending Customer Identification Program (CIP) rules to the stablecoin secondary market. In plain terms, any exchange or platform that has a direct account relationship with retail users must conduct full KYC for trading stablecoins.

The rationale is that these platforms handle most of the volume of stablecoin buy/sell transactions, yet they currently operate in a “gray area” when it comes to customer identification. BPI emphasizes that this is an anti–money laundering compliance issue. But anyone can see the implication: traditional banks want to build higher compliance walls around the stablecoin business.

Impact on the market
- Short term: Slightly bearish. BTC is consolidating around $76,948, while ETH is moving with small fluctuations of 0.63% (around $2,429). This kind of regulatory news won’t immediately crash prices, but it may dampen retail traders’ expectations of convenience in stablecoin trading. Funds may take a wait-and-see approach in the short run.
- Medium term: This is a double-edged sword. As compliance thresholds rise, smaller platforms may be forced out, while leading exchanges (such as Binance, which already does full KYC) could benefit. At the same time, traditional banks may be more willing to enter the stablecoin space—an institutionalization signal over the long run.

One-sentence translation: Banks aren’t trying to kill stablecoins—they want stablecoins to play by banks’ rules.

My take
I believe this is “short-term noise, long-term positive for institutionalization.” The clearer the regulatory framework, the more big capital will dare to move in. BTC consolidating near $76,948 is itself a sign that the market is digesting the news; if it doesn’t break down within 12 hours, it suggests the market doesn’t really care. Conversely, if ETH at $2,429 breaks below support, that would be the true signal of sentiment weakening. I’d focus on watching rather than reacting too strongly until the framework is finalized.

The U.S. has broadened the scope of its sanctions against Iran, and Tehran has issued a direct warning that it will retaliate. This kind of development appearing in crypto news is already a sign of the issue: the market is starting to worry that an escalation of conflict could spill over into commodities and risk assets. Expanded sanctions typically mean Iran’s oil exports are further constrained, tightening global crude supply and putting upward pressure on oil prices. At the same time, friction between the U.S. and China over the Iran issue could also intensify.

The transmission path is straightforward: geopolitical conflict escalates → oil prices rise → inflation expectations increase → the Fed’s rate-cut room gets squeezed → liquidity expectations deteriorate → risk assets, including crypto, face pressure. BTC is currently at $80,925.99. Although it’s still up 4.74% over the past 24h, the impact of this type of news usually shows up in prices with a lag of half a day to a day.

Market impact
- Short term: Risk-off sentiment rises, and capital flows into the U.S. dollar, gold, and U.S. Treasuries. BTC’s transmission chain is: higher oil prices boost inflation expectations → rate cuts are delayed → leveraged capital withdraws from risk assets → BTC faces selling pressure. High-beta assets like ETH $2,513.82 and BNB $717.84 typically see larger drawdowns. Watch the $78,000 support zone; a break could accelerate the decline.
- Medium term: If Iran’s retaliation stays at the verbal level, the impact may be digested within a week. Also, tense U.S.–China relations could indirectly affect the stablecoin and U.S. dollar liquidity narrative.

My take
Short-term bearish, but not panicking. The fact that it’s still up 4.74% over 24h shows buyers haven’t fully exited yet. My view: there’s a big gap between Iran’s “talk of retaliation” and “actual retaliation.” Historically, verbal threats are rarely兑现.
